evidence.quote: if disinflation and labor market conditions proceed as I am currently expecting, then some lowering of the policy rate this year would be appropriate.
I expect the disinflationary trend to continue.
That rate represents considerable progress, but it is still meaningfully above the FOMC's 2 percent target.
I expect GDP growth this year to be solid but slower than last year's strong 3.1 percent pace.
I am attentive to risks—both upside risks to my inflation outlook and downside risks to the outlook for economic activity.
As I have noted, policy is currently restrictive, and my baseline expectation is that disinflation will continue without a broad economic slowdown

parsed.rationale: The speaker expects disinflation to continue and endorses rate cuts this year, while noting that inflation is still above target and that risks run both ways. The net signal is a moderately dovish lean from restrictive policy toward easing.
